title: Sam Parr's best business books: Titan, 48 Laws, Carnegie, Sugarman, Cialdini
summary: A 2017 reading list from Sam's old blog naming the business books that shaped him. His emphasis falls on perseverance, networking by being interested in others, and copywriting and persuasion as the core skills of business. Light on tactics, but it shows what he values.

principles.text: Copywriting is the single most important skill a businessperson can have.
principles.quote: Learning how to use the written word to communicate effectively is, hands down, without a doubt, no questions asked THE most important skill any business person can have.

principles.text: Learning to influence others is essential because copywriting is the top business skill; study persuasion research.
principles.quote: Copywriting is the most important business skill you can develop. Because of that, learning how to influence others is essential.

principles.text: Perseverance is the quality most essential to success; it overcomes almost everything.
principles.quote: I do not think that there is any other quality so essential to success of any kind as the quality of perseverance. It overcomes almost everything, even nature

principles.text: Make friends by getting interested in other people rather than trying to get them interested in you.
principles.quote: You can make more friends in two months by becoming interested in other people than you can in two years by trying to get other people interested in you.

principles.text: Good copy should pull readers through it so they can't stop until they finish.
principles.quote: Your readers should be so compelled to read your copy that they cannot stop reading until they read all of it as if sliding down a slippery slope.

principles.text: Understand how power and ruthless players operate, since they can damage your career even if they self-destruct.
principles.quote: many people live by a very different set of rules, and while most of these folks eventually self-destruct, they can inflict severe damage on our personal and professional lives in the process.
